subject: Per-token delta plan: targeted benchmark & savings synthesis
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara@edgefin.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgefin.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: per-1M token delta vs hyperscalers

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the call today. To help procurement and our infra team decide, can you send a concise comparison of what we should expect for a per-1M token run (realistic numbers) and the test plan to validate claims vs the hyperscalers (we run Vertex/InferCloud currently)?

Key things they care about:
- end-to-end cost per 1M tokens for our production mix (chat + embeddings + rerank)
- assumptions about batching and cache hit rates that materially change unit costs
- what you need from us to run an apples-to-apples run (sample traces, model versions, sequence length distribution)

We need something procurement can vet this week.

—Sara
Head of Platform, EdgeFin
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@edgefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: per-1M token delta vs hyperscalers

Sara —

Appreciate the clear asks. Summary of what we discussed + proposed plan below. I kept this intentionally actionable so procurement can forward to engineering.

1) Short answer (high level):
- Expect a 25–45% effective per-1M token savings vs the hyperscaler baseline you shared when using Redwood Dedicated with: intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching (for chat), and the quantization profile we recommended. Range depends on cache hit: lower bound ~25% at 10% cache hit, upper bound ~45% at 80–90% cache hit.
- Hyperscalers often show attractive per-token model rates but don’t include the operational delta (network egress, pre/post-processing, autoscale inefficiencies, and default small-batch penalties). We’ll surface those items in the full comparison.

2) Proposed experiment (apples-to-apples):
- We run 3 controlled 1M-token passes for your workload mix:
  a) baseline: batch size 1 / no cache (hyperscaler-like small-batch)
  b) production proxy: batch size distribution you use (we’ll accept traces) + cache at observed hit rates
  c) optimized: Redwood batching + prefix cache + quantized model variant (what we expect in steady-state)
- Metrics collected: end-to-end latency P50/P95, actual GPU token cost, per-1M token invoiceable cost, and host-side CPU wall time.
- Variants: run each with cache hit rates (10%, 50%, 90%) and batch windows (1ms, 8ms, 32ms) to show sensitivity.

3) What we need from EdgeFin (minimal):
- one week of representative trace (headers: request size, seq length, request type chat/embed/rerank) — small anonymized sample is fine (we can ingest a few thousand requests). See attached: edgefin-workload-sample.json
- confirmation of the model(s) you want tested (gpt-3.5-analog / open checkpoint) or permission to mirror behavior with our closest Redwood-verified model.

4) Timeline and owners:
- Thu (today): you send trace + procurement go-ahead for test infra.
- Fri–Mon: Redwood ops runs 1M-token passes and produces the spreadsheet (redwood-1m-token-scenarios.xlsx). Owner: Ben Carter (ops contact).
- Tue: write-up + short readout call.

5) Risks / notes:
- If EdgeFin requires testing inside a VPC/on-prem replica we’ll need additional coordination and schedule — that adds 2–3 business days.
- The biggest driver is cache behavior; small changes in prefix reuse can swing delta by ~15–25%.

Next steps: If this plan looks good, reply to confirm and attach the trace. I’ll loop Marissa (AM) into procurement discussion if you want commercial framing (pilot pricing / reserved capacity options).

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@edgefin.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Re: Quick follow-up: per-1M token delta vs hyperscalers

Adding ops/bench notes so we scope the run correctly:

- For cost attribution we’ll report: GPU-hours, GPU $/hour, network egress $ (if any), and host CPU cost (approx). That lets procurement map to their TCO models.
- For sequence length distribution: please include percentiles and token histogram; if you can’t, we’ll use a conservative default (P50=64, P95=256).
- I recommend we run the optimized variant on a quantized A100 equivalent (our Dedicated profile) and the baseline on the hyperscaler SKU you use (we’ll emulate).

I’ve attached the benchmark-instr-runbook.pdf with exact commands and config we’ll run so your infra team can review.

Ben
Principal DevOps, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@edgefin.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re: Quick follow-up: per-1M token delta vs hyperscalers

Sara —

Technical clarifications from the model side:
- We’ll report per-token decode cost and also an adjusted per-inference cost that includes KV cache warm/cold factors. For rerank workloads, we’ll show both batch and unbatched numbers because rerank sometimes forces small-batch execution.
- For quantized runs: expect modest quality delta (we’ll include a short automatic sample check against your eval prompts). If you need human eval beyond that, call it out and we’ll scope.

Also: to be explicit, the caching assumptions we’ll test are: 10% (low reuse), 50% (moderate), 80% (high). If your telemetry suggests different points, tell us and we’ll add them.

Rishi
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lin <sara@edgefin.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgefin.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: per-1M token delta vs hyperscalers

Thanks — that is exactly what procurement wanted. We attached a 48‑hour sample trace (anonymized) and agreed we’ll start with the 10/50/80% cache points.

Procurement note: we also want a simple one-page comparison that lists any "hidden" costs we should be aware of (eg internal egress, cold-start penalties, minimum commitment differences). Marissa, can you coordinate commercial language and a pilot pricing line item?

Confirming timeline: we’ll send the trace now and expect your write-up on Tue. Please run the tests against the model family you suggested; we will validate quality on a 100-sample set after.

—Sara
